A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Sections and Appendices A–F can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of Pythia memorization, logistic-regression prediction results, statistical dependencies, and code-versus-natural-language memorization.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison of alternative recitation thresholds in Appendix G and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The three-category taxonomy, main duplication cutoff >5, and category-specific logistic regressions remain unchanged. Section 6 clarifies the existing prediction workflow, and Appendix G tests alternative settings without replacing the proposed method. The corrected feature criterion does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pile/Pythia memorization setting and code-versus-natural-language analyses, with BookCorpus and github-code used for classifier training. The threshold experiment adds no dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains the generic logistic-regression baseline, optimally partitioned model, and proposed taxonomic model. Figure 12 compares cutoff configurations of the existing method, rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds evaluation at duplication cutoffs >1, >5, and >10 using existing prediction metrics. Section 3.1 also changes the stated semantic-match criterion from cosine similarity ≤0.8 to ≥0.8. This is a reported setting correction; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix G and Figure 12 test sensitivity to nearby recitation thresholds, supplementing the existing KL-divergence justification and quartile-partition comparison. Earlier dependency, scaling, and code-versus-natural-language analyses remain. Table 3 removes two illustrative cases.

E5.justification: Bootstrap-based uncertainty reporting in Figures 3 and 5 and the dependency analyses are retained. No seed counts, repeated-run information, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures are added; Figure 12 supplies point estimates without uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds PR AUC, precision, recall, and ECE results across cutoff settings: >5 remains competitive but is not best on every category and metric. Table 3 removes the HarperCollins recitation example (2303 duplicates) and one numerical reconstruction example (2 duplicates). Existing Figures 2–11 and Tables 1–2 retain their results.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 reverses the inequality defining semantic-match membership from ≤0.8 to ≥0.8, a limited mathematical correction rather than equivalent notation. The k-extractability definition, taxonomic definitions, and Appendix A hashing formulation remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same taxonomy, predictive advantage, and findings about memorization across scale and training time. The revised prediction contribution clarifies its meaning without expanding its scientific claim.

C2.justification: Explanations involving rare tokens, prompt perplexity, duplication, and training dynamics remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning linear dependence and exact extraction. Appendix G supplies supporting observations for the existing cutoff without introducing a new mechanism or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies that semantic matches are counted among all 64-token Pile sequences. Conversely, v1's code-repository footnote disappears without replacement in v2. Appendix implementation details and classifier hyperparameters remain unchanged; the missing link does not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 7.1 removes 'Like us' when describing Dankers et al.'s investigation of counterfactual memorization, modestly correcting the claimed relationship to that work. The cited-work set and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include a clearer prediction contribution, an expanded explanation in Section 6, the new Appendix G, and affiliation/header edits. These are limited narrative revisions.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from two columns to the predominantly single-column ICLR layout, with resized and repositioned figures, wrapped text around Figures 3 and 6, and redistributed appendix tables. Figure 12 is added and Table 3 is shortened; existing plot content is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix G adds useful evidence for the chosen duplication cutoff, while the corrected similarity inequality and clearer prediction explanation improve accuracy and clarity. The gains are limited: the main results remain unchanged, the new comparison lacks uncertainty reporting, and removal of the code link weakens reproducibility guidance. Overall, the substantive corrections and focused validation provide a modest net improvement.
